Meeting header
Date/Time: 2025-07-19 16:30 UTC | Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Menon (Redwood SE), Evan Li (Arcadia Head of ML), Marta Gonzalez (Arcadia Platform), Samir Patel (Arcadia CTO)

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time, we'll run about 40 minutes, quick agenda — model catalog tour, how we read benchmark cards, compatibility matrix and then routing + deployment options. sound good?
00:12 Evan: yeah that sounds perfect, curious mostly about latency for generation and how to pick models that keep cost down, and also the private deployment concerns — we have strict data residency.
00:22 Priya: great — quick note, transcription may be rough, you'll see some jargon swapped — i'll try to call out the exact values as we go.
00:35 Jordan: ok i'll start with a live catalog walkthrough in the console — so top-left is the filter for objective: generation, chat, embeddings — Arcadia, for realtime customer facing chat we'll focus on generation + chat.
00:48 [screen share noise / brief pause]
01:02 Priya: pointing out the benchmark card — we show median token latency, p95, cost per 1k tokens, and quality score from small eval suites. the important bit is the compatibility matrix tab which shows what quantizations and hardware are supported — e.g., 4-bit quantized int8-ish paths, bf16, and fp16.
01:20 Marta: is that quantized 4-bit path usable on T4s or do we need A10Gs? we are mostly on mixed G4/75s in our staging.
01:31 Priya: good question — the matrix marks T4 as "limited" for some 4-bit kernels; the runtime will still serve a compatible fallback variant but latency will differ. for heavy quantization paths we recommend A100s or GA100-style tensor-core HW, or the Dedicated pool we can tune.
01:50 Evan: by fallback variant you mean it will route to a non-quantized float16 model? that could blow cost up.
02:02 Jordan: yes, routing policies are configurable — you can prefer lowest latency, prefer lowest cost, or prioritize same-region. there's also automatic fallback to a variant that is compatible with the available hardware; we can show policies shortly.
02:17 Priya: quick demo — clicking a model -> bench card -> click "compatibility matrix" — you'll see rows for quant levels: 8-bit, 4-bit, int4, and columns for instance families: T4, A10, A100, and on-prem GPUs. cells have notes like "kernel via Triton" or "soft-fallback uses bf16 path".
02:40 Samir: do you support custom kernel builds? on-prem we run a slightly patched runtime for perf.
02:46 Priya: we do an enterprise private package — that's the Private deployment mode — we can include kernel bundles and a pinned runtime image, and our compile step will select kernels during onboarding. note: kernel selection can be influenced by sequence length distributions you provide.
03:05 Jordan: switching to benchmark interpretation — the quality score is a relative metric from Redwood eval suites; it's helpful to rank models but always validate against your prompts.
03:18 Evan: can we upload our evals? we have a 2k prompt set for our agent flow.
03:24 Priya: yes, Optimize supports uploading prompt sets to run automated regressions and link quality deltas to deployments. that also feeds alerting if a rollout causes quality drift.
03:38 Marta: and for cost calculations — is cost per 1k tokens realistic for private? we have different unit economics on-prem.
03:45 Jordan: for Hosted it's per-token. for Dedicated we provide committed pricing estimates with a utilization model; for Private we provide license/ops fee plus you manage infra. We'll send a sample cost matrix that models your token mix.
03:58 Evan: what about batching — can that reduce p95 for us? our QPS is bursty.
04:06 Priya: continuous batching helps throughput but can add tail latency; Redwood Optimize suggests batching windows depending on SLO. you can set queueing policies per-route (max wait, max batch size).
04:20 Samir: show us an example of a routing policy that prefers low cost but maintains p95 under 300ms.
04:28 Priya: sure — demo time: open routing tab — policy type dropdown — choose cost-first with p95 guardrails. we add a guard: if p95 > 300ms for two consecutive 1-minute bins, route to faster variant or region. here's an example config we use in production.
04:45 [short pause, Priya typing]
05:02 Priya: note: guardrail evaluation uses recent trace stats from Console; we can evaluate across token length buckets.
05:18 Evan: curious about KV cache mentions in docs — does Redwood share KV across replicas or per-tenant?
05:25 Jordan: KV cache is per-model instance group; for Dedicated pools we can shard caches to reduce cross-tenant leakage; for Private you control isolation. caching helps prefix reuse and reduces per-token compute.
05:40 Marta: security — we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs for HIPAA. do you have SOC2 documents?
05:47 Jordan: yes — we have SOC2 excerpt in the deck; Private deployments can plug in customer KMS/HSM and we keep detailed audit logs. we'll attach the compliance pack.
06:00 Samir: on federated traffic — if region is EU, can we pin models and data to EU-only infra?
06:08 Priya: yes, region pinning is supported. routing policies include region constraints and you'd get data residency options in Private.
06:18 Evan: going back to benchmarks — can you explain how sequence length affects kernel choice?
06:25 Priya: absolutely — some kernels are optimized for short sequences (e.g., <512) and others for long sequences; the runtime's compile step picks kernels based on your expected seq distribution. we recommend uploading a sample distribution during onboarding.
06:45 Evan: if we quantize to 4-bit, do we see hallucination increase? we saw in internal tests some quality drop on few-shot tasks.
06:54 Priya: quantization can affect generation quality; Optimize will run your prompt sets across quantized and float variants and surface the delta. often 4-bit is fine for many tasks but for instruction-heavy few-shot you may prefer bf16.
07:12 Jordan: quick aside — regarding competitors, we often see folks compare to Anthropic for safety models and OpenAI for base-quality. Redwood's angle is production economics and predictable routing + fallbacks.
07:27 Marta: are there per-route overrides? our billing teams want per-team model limits.
07:31 Jordan: yes per-route quotas, token caps, and rate limits can be set in Console.
07:40 Evan: can we run a smoke benchmark in your hosted env with our prompts?
07:45 Jordan: yes — two options: 1) run a hosted benchmark using sampled tokens (we'll need sample prompts and account for rate-limits) or 2) spin a short Dedicated pilot. most folks start with hosted benchmarks and then move to Dedicated pilot if consistent.
07:58 Priya: i'll demo the benchmark runner now — choose dataset -> select model variants -> choose metrics (latency p50/p95, tokens/s, cost per 1k). clicking run.
08:12 [short spinner noise]
08:20 Priya: results will show a small table — for example your sample run shows Model-A (fp16, A100) p95 220ms cost $0.32/1k, Model-B (int4 on A100) p95 180ms cost $0.12/1k but quality delta -4% on your eval.
08:38 Evan: that's the kind of tradeoff we want to quantify — can the runner export a CSV?
08:43 Priya: yes, exportable and we can add column for sequence-length buckets.
08:50 Samir: on dedicated pools — how long to spin up a pilot and do you have minimums?
08:58 Jordan: pilots can be as short as a month; lead time depends on GPU availability. we can give a reserve estimate; we'll include that in the follow-up.
09:10 Marta: how does the A/B/canary rollout behave with model parameter changes? do you support automatic rollback?
09:20 Priya: yes — rollouts can be percent-based with automated checks: quality deltas via your eval set and latency guardrails; if thresholds breach, rollback or reroute happens automatically.
09:32 Evan: sample config?
09:35 Priya: here's an example — 10% traffic to new model, run for 30 minutes, collect p95 and quality; if quality delta > -2% or p95 increases by 20% rollback.
09:48 Jordan: will follow up with a template for canary settings.
09:52 [brief cross-talk / chair squeak]
10:05 Priya: circling back to compatibility matrix — one of the gotchas is model flavoring: a model in the catalog may have multiple build variants (fp16 baseline, q4_k, q2_k etc). the name includes the variant tag. sometimes transcription will flip q2 vs q4 in notes.
10:26 Marta: any gotchas for mixed batch sizes in production? our workloads have single-turn short chats and long multi-turn sessions.
10:35 Priya: you can route by route type — low-latency route for short chats with smaller batches and a throughput route for long sessions. prefix/KV caching reduces recompute for multi-turn.
10:50 Evan: how do we instrument to see token-level cost?
10:56 Jordan: Console traces tokens per request; we show per-route cost breakdown and token-level attribution in the billing view.
11:04 Samir: can we get a short POC scope doc — basically what success looks like in 30 days?
11:10 Jordan: yes — we'll draft a POC scope: sample prompts, SLOs, 1 or 2 models to benchmark, deployment target (hosted vs dedicated), success metrics (p95 < 300ms, quality delta < -2%, cost below target).
11:25 Evan: okay that sounds actionable.
11:28 Priya: any final questions on compatibility?
11:31 Marta: one more - when runtime chooses kernel, can we pin to a particular kernel in Private? we've got a patched kernel for some ops.
11:40 Priya: in Private yes we can use pinned kernel images; in Hosted it's managed but we can ship tuned kernels to Dedicated pools as part of enterprise onboarding.
